analysis: Examined the three modified files. ClusterPublicModels.swift adds an optional `tensorAssistant` (default nil) to ClusterPublicModel, a validated ClusterPublicTensorAssistant (requires singleton verification, a hash-shaped evidence digest, and a docs/reports/*.md path), and a `current` accessor backed by a @TaskLocal `declarationOverride`. The override is documented as test-only. In the supplied code it is only read through `current`, and nothing in the supplied evidence sets it on a product path. Every shipped `declared` model has no assistant, so behavior is unchanged today. DistributedInstalledNativeStart.resourcePolicySHA256 now appends the declared assistant's fields (schema name, depth, inventory hash, verification, evidence hash) when a declared assistant matches the artifact. Without one, the digest is byte-identical. The same function is used by the runtime block and the native authorizer `common`, so the two Macs derive the same policy. A declared assistant therefore enters the coordinator-approved resource policy, which is a fail-closed binding. publicTrafficLine now suppresses the 'assistant not offered' line only when the owner declared an assistant for that exact artifact. Display only; the line is not an enforcement path. The ClusterConfiguration.validate enforcement that the comment cites is outside the supplied evidence. The remaining questions for integration are whether ClusterConfiguration.validate and tensorAssistantServesLocally actually require the exact declared policy, and whether any non-test code sets declarationOverride. Neither is visible here, and the threat model has no directly relevant entry. This is not a finding. No regression found for T-052, T-054 or T-056 in the supplied hunks. Coverage limit: the patch_excerpt for ClusterPublicModels.swift is truncated, but the full head text was available.
